description: Ex-RAAF jet trainer; CAC-assembled. Confirmed at Point Cook by ADF-Serials (A7 page).
ADF-Serials states the museum traded Mustang A68-199 in 1998 for two WWI replicas (Avro 504K and S.E.5a) now displayed at Point Cook; treat as a replica pending museum confirmation.
RAAF elementary trainer, displayed in Hangar 180.
First RAAF Iroquois and the last B model in RAAF service; allotted to the museum 1985. ADF-Serials: currently on display at Point Cook.
Restored by No 21 (City of Melbourne) Squadron to its Battle of Long Tan configuration; relocated to Point Cook for display in 2002.
Flown to Point Cook 30 June 2007 on retirement, the last RAAF Iroquois flight; repainted for the Vietnam display.
RAAF Bristol Freighter, long-term museum exhibit.
Australian-built WWII fighter; displayed in Hangar 180.
Airworthy; civil registration VH-SVU. Operated as part of the Air Force heritage flight based at Point Cook (No 100 Squadron).
First production Winjeel; static display. ADF-Serials: on static display RAAF Museum Point Cook.
Airworthy, flying as VH-FTS with the Air Force heritage flight at Point Cook.
Prototype Avon Sabre. To Point Cook 8 November 1976 as an instructional airframe, later acquired by the museum; on static display.
Ex-US Army observation aircraft displayed in Hangar 180 wearing the marking 0-14591; RAAF/US identity not independently confirmed.
Composite airframe displayed as A24-104; built as a Canadian Vickers PBV-1A, ex-RCAF 11060, later VH-EXG.
ADF-Serials: currently on display at RAAF Museum Point Cook.
Acquired by the museum in 2005. A Tiger Moth is part of the Point Cook-based Air Force heritage flying fleet.
Displayed in the Training Hangar.
Displayed in Hangar 180.
Displayed in the Technology Hangar, painted as target tug A79-876.
Composite airframe displayed as A79-616; ADF-Serials notes the real A79-616 went to the USA and that parts of A79-827 were used in this rebuild.
ADF-Serials: currently on external display at RAAF Museum Point Cook.
Displayed in the Technology Hangar.
Australian-built target drone; ADF-Serials: on display Point Cook.
Piloted development aircraft for the Jindivik programme.
The only RAAF F-111G preserved; moved by road to Point Cook April 2009.
Displayed in Hangar 180.
Ferried to Point Cook 20 January 2004 on retirement from the School of Air Navigation, East Sale.
Outside display. ADF-Serials confirms A97-214 on outside display at Point Cook.
Joined C-130A A97-214 and C-130E A97-160 on outside display at Point Cook.
ADF-Serials: in outside storage at Point Cook, externally wrapped for corrosion protection.
Flew into Point Cook for its final landing 16 November 2017.
Displayed in the Training Hangar as Central Flying School aircraft CFS-20; original versus reproduction status not established.
Ex-USAF F-4E painted to represent the Phantoms leased by the RAAF in 1970-73 while awaiting the F-111C.
ADF-Serials: on display RAAF Museum Point Cook.
Displayed in the Training Hangar.
Replica. ADF-Serials records that the museum traded Mustang A68-199 in 1998 for two WWI replicas (Avro 504K and S.E.5a) now displayed at Point Cook.
Full-scale replica and part of the Point Cook-based Air Force heritage flying fleet (airworthy).
RAAF Seagull V / Walrus amphibian.
Full-scale flying replica built for the 1990 RAAF anniversary; flown at the 2014 Centenary of Military Aviation.
Full-scale replica of the 1910 Deperdussin, representing the type used at Point Cook in 1914.
Full-scale replica representing the Central Flying School B.E.2a of 1914.
Transferred to Air Force History and Heritage and placed on display at the RAAF Museum.
Vietnam veteran of No 2 Squadron; approved for museum display 1982. ADF-Serials: currently on display at Point Cook.
Repainted in its original blue and white scheme; final flight to retirement at the RAAF Museum 5 December 2017.
First RAAF PC-9/A; transferred to Air Force History and Heritage and displayed at the RAAF Museum.
Front fuselage only, displayed at Point Cook. The airworthy Canberra TT.18 at Temora wears these markings but is really ex-RAF WJ680.
Surface-to-air missile displayed in the Technology Hangar.
Second Bloodhound, displayed outdoors on its launcher.
Ex-RAE delta research aircraft, later ARDU; held by the museum in storage.
Winjeel prototype/pre-production airframe; ADF-Serials: currently in storage at Point Cook.
Former instructional airframe with fuselage skin removed; moved to the RAAF Museum late 2014.
Held at Point Cook painted as CA-9 A20-561; the real A20-561 was converted to components in 1946.
Long-term museum airframe; sold to a Mildura orchardist in 1954 and later recovered. Held in the museum store/restoration area.
Formerly airworthy with the RAAF Historic Flight; grounded with the wings out of fatigue life and stored at the RAAF Museum.
Flew its last flight from ARDU Edinburgh to Point Cook 19 November 1999 with 16454.1 airframe hours.
The world last flying F-111; departed Amberley by road for Point Cook 24 May 2011. ADF-Serials: currently in store at the RAAF Museum.
Ex-77 Squadron and Meteorites display team; dispatched to the RAAF Museum 17 October 1972.
On static display/store at the RAAF Museum from 15 January 1975 per ADF-Serials.
Moved to Point Cook 14 September 1971; held by the RAAF Museum.
Ex-10 Squadron maritime patrol aircraft. ADF-Serials: static display RAAF Museum Point Cook.
Ex-RAAF Ventura held by the RAAF Museum in the aircraft store.
Ex-RNZAF Harvard IIA acquired by the RAAF Museum in 1984 in a trade for Canberra A84-240.
Early RAAF helicopter held in the museum aircraft store.
Made its final flight to the RAAF Museum 17 April 2015; wrapped in a protective cocoon and stored outside. Carries nose art Lifes A Beach.
Donated 2015 as VH-FAE after long storage at Toolangi; collected by the Friends of the RAAF Museum 20 May 2015 for restoration and display as A11-17.
Former RSTT Wagga instructional airframe with fuselage skin panels removed; ADF-Serials: currently in storage at the RAAF Museum.
Transferred from RAAF Wagga to the RAAF Museum in September 2018 for restoration.
Formerly displayed outside a base building at Point Cook; ADF-Serials records it as now in storage.
